newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's Fincantieri group profit doubles in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Fincantieri group profit doubles in 1996.

text.p: Italian state shipbuilder Fincantieri said on Thursday it made a group net profit of 50.3 billion lire in 1996 against 25.2 billion the year before.
The company, part of state industrial holding IRI, said that at the parent level, it made a 66.3 billion lire profit in 1996 from 25.2 in 1995.
It said its production value rose six percent in 1996 to 3.5 trillion lire while its order book was worth some nine trillion. Group net debt at the end of last December was 340 billion lire.
Fincantieri said last year that it expected to post stronger 1996 results mainly because of a rigorous cost-cutting policy linked to the company's strength in the cruise liner sector.
It said on Thursday that it had recently signed deals to build two large cruise ships, one for Carnival Corp and the other for P&O Cruises. -- Rome newsroom +396 6782501
